title: IC 1396A Elephant Trunk Nebula
caption: The Elephant Trunk Nebula (IC 1396A), imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This image focuses on IC 1396A, a dense, dark cloud of gas sitting inside a much larger glowing nebula. Its distinctive shape has earned it the informal name Elephant Trunk Nebula.

The larger nebula, IC 1396, is a giant emission nebula more than 3 degrees across on the sky. Its light comes from HD 206267, a hot and massive O-type star close to the nebula's centre. That star lies just beyond the top edge of this frame, so it does not appear here.

An emission nebula glows because intense light from hot stars energises its gas. Dense clouds like the Elephant Trunk resist that light for longer than the thinner gas around them, so they stand out as dark shapes silhouetted against the glow.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope used three filters. Hydrogen-alpha is shown in red, sulphur [S II] in blue and the I filter in orange.
filters: 672 nm · Optical Sll (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
805 nm · Optical I (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
656 nm · Optical Ha (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
understand.eye: The I filter reaches into near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and narrow filters isolate the faint glow of individual gases.

explore: The image comes from the wide-field Mosaic camera on Kitt Peak National Observatory's Mayall 4-meter telescope. North is to the right and east is up. The same gallery holds images of other parts of IC 1396.
alt: A dark, dense cloud with a trunk-like shape set within glowing nebulosity.
